api.description:
Make an authenticated HTTP request to a Sanity API

The endpoint argument is an API path as documented in the published OpenAPI
specifications - list them with "sanity openapi list" and inspect one with
"sanity openapi get <slug>". Paths can be copied verbatim from the specs:
{projectId} and {dataset} placeholders are filled in from flags or the CLI
configuration, and the API host (api.sanity.io or <projectId>.api.sanity.io)
is chosen based on the specs' routing information.

The default request method is GET, or POST when fields or --input are
provided. For GET/HEAD requests, fields are sent as query parameters;
otherwise they are combined into a JSON request body sent with
"Content-Type: application/json". Raw --input bodies are sent without a
default Content-Type - provide one with -H when the API requires it. The
response body is written to stdout.

Requests are authenticated with the token from "sanity login". To use a
specific token instead - for example in CI or when the CLI is not logged in
- pass --token or set the SANITY_AUTH_TOKEN environment variable. Pass
--anonymous to send no token at all.

new.description:
Sets up two folders here: ./sanity, a Studio where you write and edit your
content, and ./web, a Next.js website that reads it. Both are already
connected to your new project, so you can start them straight away. Use
--no-scaffold if you just want the project and nothing else.

The project is real and works immediately, but it is only yours for 72 hours.
Claim it with a Sanity account before the deadline and everything you have
built stays exactly as it is. Claiming is free and takes about a minute. Miss
the deadline and the project and its content are deleted.

Two things to keep private: the claim link, because anyone who opens it
becomes the owner, and the access token saved in ./sanity/.env.local, because
it can read and change everything in the project. ./web/.env.local has only
the project ID and dataset. Keep both env files out of git, and never put the
token in code that runs in the browser.

Run this command with --instructions for the full agent setup guide.

typegen:generate.description:
Sanity TypeGen

Configuration:
This command can utilize configuration settings defined in a `sanity-typegen.json` file. These settings include:

- "path": Specifies a glob pattern to locate your TypeScript or JavaScript files.
  Default: "./src/**/*.{ts,tsx,js,jsx}"

- "schema": Defines the path to your Sanity schema file. This file should be generated using the `sanity schema extract` command.
  Default: "schema.json"

- "generates": Indicates the path where the generated TypeScript type definitions will be saved.
  Default: "./sanity.types.ts"

The default configuration values listed above are used if not overridden in your `sanity-typegen.json` configuration file. To customize the behavior of the type generation, adjust these properties in the configuration file according to your project's needs.

Note:
- The `sanity schema extract` command is a prerequisite for extracting your Sanity Studio schema into a `schema.json` file, which is then used by the `sanity typegen generate` command to generate type definitions.
- To generate types for several datasets, list them in `typegen.resources` in `sanity.cli.ts` (beta). Each resource uses its own `schema` file, or the schema bound to its dataset when `schema` is omitted. With `--watch`, a schema bound to a dataset is fetched once, when the watcher starts. Restart it after deploying a schema.

context:sources:create.description:
Adds a source to a knowledge base. Set `type` to choose what it reads:

- `web`: a website, crawled from `url`
- `sanity-dataset`: the documents a GROQ query selects in a Sanity dataset
- `files`: files you upload with `POST .../sources/{sourceId}/uploads`, or text you send in `content`

A website or dataset starts its first sync right away. A `files` source syncs when you upload a file, or right away when you send `content`: one request stores the text, adds the source and starts its sync. For a website, set `dryRun` to `true` to preview the crawl without adding the source.

Adding a website that is already a source returns `409` with code `webSourceRootConflict`, and adding more websites than your limit allows returns `409` with code `webSourceRootLimitExceeded`. When the organization's knowledge bases already hold as many source chunks as its plan allows, returns `403` with code `planLimitReached` and adds nothing. Supports the `Idempotency-Key` header.

context:sources:edit.description:
Changes a source's title, a website's crawl options, a dataset's query, or how often a website or dataset syncs on its own. New crawl options delete the documents whose path they leave out. When that would delete all of the source's documents, or five or more that are over a fifth of them, the request returns `409` with code `sourceDeletionsUnconfirmed` until you send it again with `confirmDeletions` set to `true`. New crawl options sent while the source syncs return `409` with code `syncInProgress`; send them again once the sync finishes. A new query queues a sync, which removes the documents the query no longer selects.

Crawl options on a source that isn't a website, a query on one that isn't a dataset, or a sync frequency on a `files` source, return `422` with code `sourceTypeMismatch`. Setting a sync frequency on a plan without scheduled syncs returns `403` with code `featureNotInPlan`; setting it to `null` always works.

context:sources:sync.description:
Starts a sync of the source. A website or dataset is read again: its sync is queued, and starts once any sync of the source that is running ends, including the first one that started when it was added. Asking again while one waits queues nothing more. Follow it with the source's `latestSync`.

For a `files` source, set `uploadId` to the upload whose file the source should hold from now on; without it, the source reads its current file again. Its sync starts at once and returns a job ID to poll; the finished job's `result` names the sync and whether it is `held`. While a sync of a `files` source is running, including the first one, the request returns `409` with code `syncInProgress` and leaves the upload for a later request. An `uploadId` whose file never arrived returns `404` with code `uploadNotFound`, and an `uploadId` on a source that isn't `files` returns `422` with code `sourceTypeMismatch`.

Supports the `Idempotency-Key` header.
